newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Bre-X hits Randgold's London share debut.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bre-X hits Randgold's London share debut.

text.p: The London debut of South Africa's Randgold Resources Ltd and its share offer failed to meet market expectations on Thursday as investors were still reluctant to put money in gold projects in the aftermath of the Bre-X scandal.

Randgold Resources, part of Randgold and Exploration Company Ltd, said it issued fewer shares at a lower price than it had initially envisaged, but still called its London-listing "satisfactory" in the light of the recent upheaval in gold markets.
Bre-X, a small Canadian mining firm, rocked world markets as it emerged in May that its claims of having found this century's biggest gold deposit were based on a massive fraud.
Gold prices have plummeted and investors immediately shunned exploration projects.
Against this backdrop, Randgold, which needs money to develop projects in Mali and Tanzania, raised $82.5 million, while it had originally hoped to find $125 million or more.
"This shows a sick gold market. It was unfortunate timing, but the company had to do it sooner rather than later," said analyst Roger Chaplin at broker T.Hoare.
The share offer's proceeds will go towards funding the capital expenditure programme at the Randgold Resources' Syama gold mine in Mali and repayment of a loan assumed when it bought Syama last year.
It will also be used to develop the Loulo mine in Mali and pay for a bankable feasibility study for the Golden Ridge project in Tanzania.

Randgold Resources said the share offer failed to meet its "ambitious" targets, but managing director Mark Bristow added: "The outcome was satisfactory considering the adverse circumstances which had developed since it (Randgold) had embarked on this exercise."
Analysts, meanwhile, reckon Randgold Resources will tap the London market again at a later stage when the Bre-X shockwaves have been fully absorbed.
Randgold Resources' London debut comes about a week after another South African firm, Gencor Ltd, announced it would float its base metals arm on the stock exchange here.
The Billiton float is set to raise over $1 billion in an equity placement in July with share trading beginning the following month.
But Billiton is unlikely to suffer from the Bre-X debacle. Instead, analysts said earlier it was well positioned to buy small mining operations which may currently be undervalued.
Randgold Resources shares closed at $16.75 compared with a $16.50 offer price.
The company earlier said it aimed to offer the stocks between $18-$23 per share. A total of five million share were issued compared with seven million as originally planned.
